[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "Random Experiments, Outcomes, and Sample Spaces",
    "scope": "Introduces the foundational objects of probability theory from physical reality to formal mathematical abstraction. Classifies sample spaces by cardinality into finite, countably infinite, and uncountably infinite (continuous) domains with physical examples. Details the granularity principle, demonstrating how multiple valid sample spaces of differing resolution can model the same physical experiment.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definitions of random experiment, elementary outcome (sample point) $\\omega$, and sample space $S$ (or $\\Omega$)",
      "Properties of sample space elements: mutual exclusivity and collective exhaustiveness",
      "Cardinality taxonomy: finite ($|S| < \\infty$, e.g., coin tosses, dice rolls), countably infinite ($|S| = \\aleph_0$, e.g., email arrivals, trials until success), and uncountably infinite ($|S| = 2^{\\aleph_0}$, e.g., resistor voltage, electronic component lifespan $[0, \\infty)$, particle position $\\mathbb{R}^3$)",
      "Granularity principle: choice of sample space based on experimental inquiry level (e.g., exact die faces $S_1 = \\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\\}$ vs. parity $S_2 = \\{\\text{even}, \\text{odd}\\}$)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Events and Set-Theoretic Operations",
    "scope": "Defines events as subsets of the sample space, distinguishing between simple, compound, certain, and null/impossible events. Formalizes standard set operations (union, intersection, complement, difference, symmetric difference) in the language of probability, and rigorously establishes Boolean event identities including De Morgan's laws via element-chasing proofs.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definition of an event $A \\subseteq S$, occurrence criterion $\\omega \\in A$, certain event $S$, and impossible/null event $\\emptyset$",
      "Classification: simple/elementary events (singletons $\\{\\omega\\}$) versus compound events",
      "Event operations and logical equivalents: union $A \\cup B$ ('at least one'), intersection $A \\cap B$ ('both'), complement $A^c$ or $A'$ ('not $A$'), set difference $A \\setminus B = A \\cap B^c$ ('$A$ but not $B$'), and symmetric difference $A \\Delta B = (A \\setminus B) \\cup (B \\setminus A)$ ('exactly one')",
      "Mutually exclusive (disjoint) events: $A \\cap B = \\emptyset$",
      "Boolean algebra identities: absorption, complementation ($A \\cup A^c = S$, $A \\cap A^c = \\emptyset$, $(A^c)^c = A$), and rigorous element-chasing proof of De Morgan's laws: $(A \\cap B)^c = A^c \\cup B^c$ and $(\\bigcap_{i=1}^n A_i)^c = \\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i^c$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Empirical and Classical Probability",
    "scope": "Explores the earliest operational definitions of probability and their practical limitations. Develops the frequentist concept via empirical proportions and relative frequency stabilization, and formalizes the classical discrete probability model on finite uniform spaces, including combinatorial selection without replacement.",
    "key_points": [
      "Empirical (relative frequency) probability: $P_n(A) = m/n$, empirical stabilization phenomenon as $n \\to \\infty$, and experimental error bounds across trial magnitudes ($10^2, 10^4, 10^6$)",
      "Limitation of empirical approach: relies on infinitely repeatable, identical trials",
      "Classical probability definition for equiprobable finite sample spaces: $\\mathbb{P}(A) = \\frac{|A|}{|S|} = \\frac{m}{n}$",
      "Discrete sample point weight assignment: $P(A) = \\sum_{\\omega \\in A} w_\\omega$ where $\\sum_{\\omega \\in S} w_\\omega = 1$, loaded die and biased outcome formulations",
      "Combinatorial evaluation on uniform spaces: sampling without replacement using binomial coefficients $\\binom{N}{k}$, defect/quality control distributions"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Geometric Probability Models",
    "scope": "Extends the classical concept of equiprobable outcomes to continuous spaces of length, area, and volume in $\\mathbb{R}^n$. Teaches the setup, boundary condition translation, and geometric calculation for the classic Meeting Problem (including arbitrary waiting time $t$) and the Broken Stick Problem for forming a triangle.",
    "key_points": [
      "Geometric probability definition: $\\mathbb{P}(A) = \\frac{\\text{measure}(A)}{\\text{measure}(S)}$ for measurable subsets $A \\subseteq S \\subset \\mathbb{R}^n$ (length in $\\mathbb{R}$, area in $\\mathbb{R}^2$, volume in $\\mathbb{R}^3$)",
      "The Meeting Problem: uniform arrival times $(x, y) \\in [0, T]^2$, arrival constraint $|x - y| \\le t$, complement area computation via corner right triangles, and solving for threshold waiting time $t$ such that $\\mathbb{P}(A_t) \\ge p$",
      "The Broken Stick Problem: uniform break points $x, y \\sim \\text{Uniform}[0, 1]$, translation of triangle inequalities (each side $< 1/2$) into planar geometric regions, and area computation of favorable symmetric simplices yielding $\\mathbb{P} = 1/4$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "$\\sigma$-Algebras and Measurable Spaces",
    "scope": "Provides the mathematical motivation for restricting the domain of probability measures beyond naive power sets on infinite spaces. Formulates the axioms of a $\\sigma$-algebra, introduces the concept of a measurable space $(S, \\mathcal{F})$, and builds a comprehensive zoo of fundamental $\\sigma$-algebras including those generated by finite partitions and continuous generators.",
    "key_points": [
      "Motivation: non-measurability pathologies preventing probability assignment to all subsets of uncountable spaces",
      "Definition of a $\\sigma$-algebra $\\mathcal{F}$: contains the whole space $S$, closed under complementation, and closed under countable unions",
      "Measurable space definition: the mathematical pair $(S, \\mathcal{F})$",
      "Catalog of $\\sigma$-algebras: trivial/minimal $\\mathcal{F}_0 = \\{\\emptyset, S\\}$, discrete/power set $\\mathcal{P}(S) = 2^S$, generated by a single proper event $\\{\\emptyset, A, A^c, S\\}$, and countable-cocountable $\\sigma$-algebra on uncountable sets",
      "Generation by finite partitions: definition of atoms, partition into $n$ parts yielding a finite $\\sigma$-algebra of exactly $2^n$ sets",
      "Borel $\\sigma$-algebra $\\mathcal{B}(\\mathbb{R})$ generated by open intervals $\\{(a, b) : a < b\\}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Algebraic Properties of $\\sigma$-Algebras",
    "scope": "Investigates the behavior of $\\sigma$-algebras under standard set-system operations. Proves that the arbitrary intersection of $\\sigma$-algebras is always a $\\sigma$-algebra, and constructs explicit counterexamples proving that the union of two $\\sigma$-algebras is generally not a $\\sigma$-algebra due to failure of union closure.",
    "key_points": [
      "Theorem: If $\\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\\mathcal{F}_2$ are $\\sigma$-algebras on $X$, then $\\mathcal{F}_1 \\cap \\mathcal{F}_2$ is a $\\sigma$-algebra on $X$",
      "Rigorous proof of intersection closure across the three defining axioms: preservation of $X$, closure under complements, and closure under countable unions",
      "Non-closure of unions: analysis of why $\\mathcal{F}_1 \\cup \\mathcal{F}_2$ fails to be a $\\sigma$-algebra",
      "Canonical counterexample on $X = \\{1, 2, 3\\}$ with $\\mathcal{F}_1 = \\{\\emptyset, \\{1\\}, \\{2, 3\\}, X\\}$ and $\\mathcal{F}_2 = \\{\\emptyset, \\{2\\}, \\{1, 3\\}, X\\}$, demonstrating that $\\{1\\} \\cup \\{2\\} = \\{1, 2\\} \\notin \\mathcal{F}_1 \\cup \\mathcal{F}_2$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Kolmogorov's Axioms and the Probability Space",
    "scope": "Establishes the modern axiomatic foundation of probability theory via the Kolmogorov axioms. Defines a probability measure and the complete probability space triple $(S, \\mathcal{F}, \\mathbb{P})$, and demonstrates rigorous verification techniques to determine whether candidate set functions satisfy or violate specific axioms.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definition of a probability measure $\\mathbb{P}: \\mathcal{F} \\to [0, 1]$",
      "Kolmogorov Axiom 1 (Non-negativity): $\\mathbb{P}(A) \\ge 0$ for all $A \\in \\mathcal{F}$",
      "Kolmogorov Axiom 2 (Normalization): $\\mathbb{P}(S) = 1$",
      "Kolmogorov Axiom 3 (Countable Additivity): $\\mathbb{P}\\left(\\bigcup_{i=1}^\\infty A_i\\right) = \\sum_{i=1}^\\infty \\mathbb{P}(A_i)$ for pairwise disjoint $A_i \\cap A_j = \\emptyset$ ($i \\ne j$)",
      "Definition and structure of the probability space $(S, \\mathcal{F}, \\mathbb{P})$",
      "Axiomatic verification diagnostics: identifying specific failure modes (non-negativity violations, defective or excessive normalization sums, failure of additivity under non-linear weight assignments such as $(|A|/n)^2$)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "title": "Fundamental Consequences of the Kolmogorov Axioms",
    "scope": "Derives the core algebraic theorems of probability directly from Kolmogorov's axioms without extraneous assumptions. Provides full proofs for the probability of the impossible event, the complement rule, monotonicity, subset difference, finite additivity, and Boole's inequality (union bound).",
    "key_points": [
      "Theorem and proof: $\\mathbb{P}(\\emptyset) = 0$ via countable additivity on $S = S \\cup \\emptyset$",
      "Theorem and proof: $\\mathbb{P}(A^c) = 1 - \\mathbb{P}(A)$ via disjoint decomposition $S = A \\cup A^c$",
      "Theorem and proof of Monotonicity: if $A \\subseteq B$, then $\\mathbb{P}(A) \\le \\mathbb{P}(B)$, derived via disjoint decomposition $B = A \\sqcup (B \\setminus A)$ and non-negativity",
      "Subset difference identity: $\\mathbb{P}(B \\setminus A) = \\mathbb{P}(B) - \\mathbb{P}(A)$ for $A \\subseteq B$, and general form $\\mathbb{P}(A \\setminus B) = \\mathbb{P}(A) - \\mathbb{P}(A \\cap B)$",
      "Finite additivity: $\\mathbb{P}\\left(\\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\\right) = \\sum_{i=1}^n \\mathbb{P}(A_i)$ for pairwise disjoint collections",
      "Boole's inequality (Union Bound): $\\mathbb{P}\\left(\\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\\right) \\le \\sum_{i=1}^n \\mathbb{P}(A_i)$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "title": "Inclusion-Exclusion Principles and Event Decompositions",
    "scope": "Develops the addition rules for overlapping events and generalizes them to arbitrary unions. Details the inclusion-exclusion theorem for two and three events with set-theoretic and Venn diagram proofs, and establishes decomposition formulas for complex joint events including 'at least one', 'none', 'at least two', and 'exactly one'.",
    "key_points": [
      "Theorem and proof of the Addition Rule for two arbitrary events: $\\mathbb{P}(A \\cup B) = \\mathbb{P}(A) + \\mathbb{P}(B) - \\mathbb{P}(A \\cap B)$, reducing to simple additivity when disjoint",
      "Inclusion-Exclusion theorem for three events: $\\mathbb{P}(A \\cup B \\cup C) = \\sum \\mathbb{P}(A_i) - \\sum_{i<j} \\mathbb{P}(A_i \\cap A_j) + \\mathbb{P}(A \\cap B \\cap C)$",
      "De Morgan representations for joint non-occurrence ('none of them occurs'): $\\mathbb{P}(A^c \\cap B^c \\cap C^c) = 1 - \\mathbb{P}(A \\cup B \\cup C)$",
      "Formulas for structured combinations: $\\mathbb{P}(\\text{at least two}) = \\sum_{i<j} \\mathbb{P}(A_i \\cap A_j) - 2\\mathbb{P}(A \\cap B \\cap C)$ and $\\mathbb{P}(\\text{exactly one}) = \\mathbb{P}(\\bigcup A_i) - \\mathbb{P}(\\text{at least two})$",
      "Symmetric difference probability: $\\mathbb{P}(A \\Delta B) = \\mathbb{P}(A \\cup B) - \\mathbb{P}(A \\cap B) = \\mathbb{P}(A \\setminus B) + \\mathbb{P}(B \\setminus A)$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "title": "Probability on Discrete Infinite Spaces and Measure Validity",
    "scope": "Examines probability measures defined on countably infinite sample spaces, focusing on convergence conditions and infinite series summation. Contrasts legitimate countably additive discrete models with non-standard set functions that violate additivity.",
    "key_points": [
      "Formulation of probability measures on $S = \\{1, 2, 3, \\dots\\}$ via infinite series: $\\sum_{k=1}^\\infty p_k = 1$",
      "Geometric decay weight model $\\mathbb{P}(\\{k\\}) = c / 3^k$: solving for normalization constant $c = 2$ using infinite geometric series $\\sum_{k=1}^\\infty r^k = \\frac{r}{1 - r}$",
      "Calculating event probabilities on infinite discrete spaces: even-number events via ratio $1/9$ and tail events $\\mathbb{P}(k \\ge K)$ via complement summation",
      "Pathology of non-countably-additive set functions: evaluation of $Q(A) = 0$ (for finite $A$) and $1$ (for infinite $A$), proving breakdown of finite additivity on complementary infinite sets and catastrophic breakdown of countable additivity on singleton partitions"
    ]
  }
]
